findings.where: First screen, the hero ground behind the heading, notes, actions and portrait (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The hero sits on a pale blue-to-lilac gradient, not the warm paper used everywhere else. The page's own palette panel says the page has only three colours, no accent, and a flat warm paper with no texture. The violet is outside the house colours, and the hero is the one place the page breaks its own rule. The gradient also starts and stops sharply: under the paper header bar, and on the phone it stops in a hard line before the paper below.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for one soft ground with the house blue and grey as the only ink, and a warm paper. Mark, because a lilac wash reads as a software start-up rather than a lawyer's brief. A bank officer, who sees an off-brand colour on the first screen that appears nowhere else.

findings.where: First screen, the action row: 'Write to me' and 'Book a consultation'
findings.fault: Two identical filled house-blue rectangles sit side by side, so the action fill no longer marks a single action. One of them, 'Write to me', is not a control: it is a label in a button's fill, and only the address beside it, which is not a link either, says how to write. The blue fill means 'press here' on one box and is only a label on the other.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a development bank, who clicks 'Write to me' and nothing happens, and who cannot tell which blue box is the way to reach Mark. The founder, whose brief asks for one direct, personal action on the first screen.

findings.where: Margin notes beside the hero (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024) and the blue section labels down the left of the specimen (Palette, Type, Texture, Article page, Motion, Tile notes)
findings.fault: The house blue does four jobs at once: wordmark, static margin notes, links and the action. The notes are lecture titles set in link blue, so they look like links to those talks, but none of them goes anywhere. Nothing in the colour tells a reader what can be clicked and what cannot.
findings.who_objects: A bank officer who wants to see the Istanbul or Melbourne talk, clicks the blue title and gets nothing, and then distrusts the other blue text.

findings.where: Hero portrait and the motion sketch's exhibit photo, compared with the article page's radio-interview photo
findings.fault: The hero portrait sits on a wide, soft drop shadow that floats it off the page, even though it is a static photograph. The article photograph has no shadow, so the two photographs are framed differently. On the lilac ground the shadow also picks up a bluish cast.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the founder, who need one rule for how a photograph sits on the page. A careful reader, who sees a lifted card that does nothing when clicked.

findings.where: Article page, the 'Download' button on the PDF row, compared with the hero's buttons
findings.fault: The download is an outlined capsule with a thin blue edge, while the hero's actions are square-cornered filled blocks. The page's actions use two corner shapes and two treatments, with nothing to say why.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether the tile is one consistent system Angélique can reuse. A visitor, who sees two unrelated button styles on one page.
